decisions_made: Per the delegation's continuation note, started with ChronicleToCountermodel.lean (137 lines, next count-2-tier target per smaller-files-first), worked down the count-2 tier's 9 smallest files, then continued opportunistically into the count-1 tier once useful, per the cycle-22-established heuristic that small line count is a stronger effort predictor than tier once past the count-3 tier.

For Correctness.lean's paired unusedSectionVars/unusedDecidableInType warnings on decide_sound, used `omit [DecidableEq Atom] [Hashable Atom] in` rather than two separate narrowings, since removing the genuinely-unused section variable also eliminates the hypothesis the second linter was complaining about -- verified this matches an existing established pattern elsewhere in the codebase (SignedFormula.lean, BDriver.lean) before applying it.

For InteriorOperators.lean's 5 linter.style.show warnings (each explicitly reporting 'this tactic invocation changed the goal'), replaced show with change rather than narrowing the suppression -- change is the tactic show is discouraged from doing implicitly when a defeq change occurs, so this is a semantically-identical rename, not a proof-term alteration; verified via rebuild after each replacement.

For ChronicleToCountermodel.lean's single bare-simp linter.flexible site, took the linter's own 'Try this: simp only [ne_eq, Subtype.mk.injEq]' suggestion verbatim rather than manually reconstructing -- verified it closed the goal identically via rebuild.

Inspected but deliberately did NOT touch two files whose sole remaining suppression is a pre-existing, explicitly-commented permanent exception: Conversions.lean (linter.privateModule, a proof_wanted-only file with nothing to attach a narrower suppression to) and DefectChain.lean (linter.style.openClassical, a file-wide open Classical whose declaration-scoped equivalent would silently break Finset.filter's instance propagation per the file's own comment). Both are recorded in the plan as permanent end states, matching QLemma.lean/Eliminations.lean's existing documented pattern, so future cycles do not re-attempt them.

Verified Bimodal/ProofSystem/Derivation.lean (a heavily-imported core DerivationTree base type with dozens of transitive importers) via a full `lake build` (3309/3309, exactly the 5 documented baseline sorry warnings, zero new) rather than attempting to enumerate every downstream importer individually -- judged this an acceptable, faster substitute verification method for this specific case, and recorded it as a new finding for future cycles facing similarly foundational files.

Re-baselined check-lint-suppressions.sh once at cycle end (covering all 17 files in one baseline commit) rather than per-file, consistent with cycle 22's own established practice for this step and verified the ratchet gate still reports a clean, monotonically-decreasing result (60, baseline ceiling 60) rather than leaving the gain unlocked.

Fully rewrote the plan's RESUME HERE section rather than appending another entry on top of the existing one, per the standing instruction that the resume point must be complete and cold-startable -- prior RESUME HERE entries are preserved in git history, not lost. Also updated the plan header, Phase 5 heading stats, and the Definition-of-Done suppression-audit criterion, all of which had gone stale after cycle 22.

Did not re-investigate Phase 7's two former blockers (both CLOSED by explicit user decision in commit 5d58795c prior to this dispatch) and corrected the stale text noting they remained open where it appeared in the plan header, matching this dispatch's explicit instruction not to carry them forward as open in this handoff.
